data.exact_reserve_text: Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 & prior (2013 - 2010 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 41.2m (2013-GBP 28.7m).

prior_year_events.impact_description: costs to remove the Costa Concordia increased twice during the year, adding a further US$315m to the overall cost! (approx. GBP 192.1m strengthening)
further deterioration in the P&I claim for the Rena (which grounded and broke up offshore New Zealand in October 2011). The total P&l claim is now $425m (approx. GBP 259.2m strengthening)

syndicate also suffered two notable claims on its US P&C account from the back years. Despite specific losses, the US P&C account has made its first profit for a couple of years and is expected to go from strength to strength, indicating overall favorable development.

named_events.loss_description: The year was benign from a loss standpoint with the only major loss being Hurricane Sandy.
costs to remove the Costa Concordia increased twice during the year, adding a further US$315m to the overall cost!
further deterioration in the P&I claim for the Rena (which grounded and broke up offshore New Zealand in October 2011). The total P&l claim is now $425m.

disappearance of flight MH370. Syndicate agreed to fund 50% of the loss with Hull All Risk insurers paying the other 50%. Estimated net loss to syndicate $6.7m (war policy) + $3.5m (aviation reinsurance).
shooting down of MH17 over the Ukraine. Estimated net loss to syndicate $10.8m gross and $9.8m net.
destruction of several aircraft during intense fighting at Tripoli airport. Estimated market loss $600m-$700m, syndicate loss less than 1% of total claim.
Marine War loss when a dredger 'sucked up' an old mine which subsequently exploded, damaging the ship.
One of the largest losses from Hurricane Odile in Mexico, in the region of $5m.
One of the largest losses from flooding in Detroit, in the region of $5m.
One of the largest losses from a Satellite launch loss, in the region of $5m.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 609 reported a favorable prior year development of GBP 41.2 million for underwriting years 2011 and prior, resulting from a reassessment of claims outstanding. This release contributed to the overall syndicate profit. While the overall development was favorable, specific prior year events like the Costa Concordia (2012) and Rena (2011) experienced significant adverse development, with increased costs and deterioration in claims. The US P&C account also saw notable claims from back years, but overall achieved a profit. The report also details several significant named events impacting the 2013 and 2014 underwriting years, including the disappearance of Flight MH370, the shooting down of MH17, destruction of aircraft at Tripoli airport, a Marine War loss, Hurricane Odile, Detroit flooding, and a Satellite launch loss.
